A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 17-page versions of the same ∞-VIDEO paper. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of the proposed ∞-VIDEO variants in Tables 1–3, attention visualizations, and MovieChat ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative and ablation results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same continuous attention, memory consolidation, sticky sampling, STM/LTM weighting, and running-average aggregation. The tensor-dimension correction in Section 3.4 does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate NeXT-QA, EgoSchema, Video-MME, and MovieChat-1K and include the same trailer and movie examples. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each of Tables 1–3, including MovieChat, MovieChat+, VideoChat, Video-ChatGPT, and the Video-MME baselines. Table 1 only corrects the capitalization of Video LLaMA.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same frame/chunk configurations, model variants, evaluation metrics, answer-selection procedures, and GPT-3.5 evaluation prompts. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The STM/LTM comparisons, Appendix B.1 ablations of memory weighting and basis-function count, and attention/frame-selection analyses in Section 4.4 and Appendix B.2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate tables and ablation curves without error bars. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the discussion of GPT evaluator variability is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and Appendix B retain the same results and findings. For example, sticky ∞-Video LLaMA still reports 41.1 on NeXT-QA, 46.8 on EgoSchema, and 72.2 accuracy on MovieChat.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the declared shape of Z_STM from M × d to R × d, using the number of query tokens rather than frames per chunk. This is a local mathematical dimension correction; the remaining equations and mathematical development are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, single-pass long-video understanding through continuous-time memory and the same claimed empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations involving training-data differences, attention decay, and architecture-dependent STM/LTM benefits. The cognitive interpretations, future directions, and surveillance/bias caveats are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same implementation descriptions, checkpoints, hyperparameters, numerical integration settings, evaluation prompts, and reported code/model links. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to ∞-former and the distinctions from MovieChat and MovieChat+. Bibliographic content is retained despite pagination changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds an ICML 2025 proceedings/copyright notice and corrects 'Video LLaMa' to 'Video LLaMA' in Table 1. The prose and section order otherwise remain effectively unchanged.

P2.justification: The publication notice and associated reflow shift text across columns and pages, and the introductory motivating question becomes italicized. Figures and table structures are retained; Appendix A–B pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: Correcting Z_STM to R × d in Section 3.4 makes its declared shape consistent with the query-token output described in Section 2.3, modestly improving mathematical clarity. The experimental evidence, claims, and appendices remain unchanged, and the other edits are primarily publication formatting.
